requirements.description: Discover valid AWS resource identifiers from the current account/region using only curated read actions, bounded requests and literal dependencies
evidence: Declarative discovery covers 125/150 curated actions through 82 discovery rules; rules are validated against the curated catalog and botocore request models.
Discovery requests are bounded, dependency-aware and routed through read_action so aws.read permission, account/region context and read-only action enforcement remain centralized.

requirements.description: Inspect metadata for a selected AWS resource through explicit read-only actions before applying it to a runbook
evidence: 26 declarative inspection rules expose selected-resource metadata through explicit user-triggered read-only actions.
Resource selection and application remain separate operations in the Streamlit picker.

requirements.description: Expose DynamoDB keys/indexes clearly without pretending DynamoDB has a relational column schema
evidence: DynamoDB authoring exposes table keys plus GSI/LSI metadata from DescribeTable.
Optional observed-field sampling uses an explicit read-only Scan with Limit=10 and no automatic pagination; UI states that sampled attributes are not table schema.

requirements.description: Preserve manual fallback, RBAC, account/region scope, no implicit AWS calls and no automatic mutation
evidence: Manual fallback remains available when discovery is unavailable or intentionally skipped.
Discovery and inspection are explicit user actions and use the existing governed read path; no real AWS mutation was introduced or executed.

requirements.description: Validate provider rules, Streamlit behavior, full Python quality suite and authoring browser journey without real AWS calls
evidence: Final consolidated local gate: 358 passed, 197 subtests passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed, coverage 96.44%, exit code 0.
Focused discovery/resource-picker/DynamoDB tests passed; all four browser gates in the local quality workflow passed.
Ruff, format, mypy (70 source files), Bandit, React tests/build, npm audit and isolated pip-audit are green.
